notes: Pre-registered hypothesis VALIDATED: BMAD's full Analyst→PM→Architect→PO→SM→Dev→QA chain surfaced 7/7 requirements bullets (the maximum), including the /health exclusion that BOTH A3 and B3 missed conceptually. PRD explicitly states 'GET /health SHALL be exempt from rate limiting' as an assumption with an open question for ratification, plus fail-open semantics under concurrent load, plus env-var configurability (RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS/WINDOW_SECONDS). Implementation has the most thoughtful identity model of the three: user:<id> if X-User-Id present, else ip:<host> — handles both auth and anon (A3 was IP-only, B3 was user-only with anon bypass). Threading-safe lock (vs A3's asyncio-only assumption). 19/19 tests pass. Cost $4.58 = 8× A3 ($0.57) and 1.6× B3 ($2.84); duration 1174s = ~5× A3 and ~1.7× B3. Worth it on this task.
